citation.title: Reinforcement learning-based topology optimization for generative designed lightweight structures
citation.authors: Keerthi Kumar N, Manasa C M, Pavan Kumar B K, Manish Bali
citation.version_coded: version of record, Europe PMC full-text XML

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The PPO design reportedly reduces weight by as much as 40% relative to conventional SIMP and level-set approaches while retaining structural compliance.
claim.key_phrase: up to 40 % weight reduction while maintaining compliance
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Method validation, inference-time comparison near Fig. 12: SIMP approximately 18.4 s / PPO approximately 2.1 s = approximately 8.76.
claim.alternatives: Method validation near Fig. 12 compares approximate inference times of PPO 2.1 s and SIMP 18.4 s; the abstract also asserts rapid design-to-prototype transition.

baseline.classical_method: SIMP and level set named in abstract; SIMP timed in Method validation near Fig. 12
baseline.problem_size: Method details, Table 1: 60 x 40 grid, 2400 elements, 2D cantilever
baseline.classical_time: Method validation near Fig. 12: approximately 18.4 s for SIMP
baseline.ml_time: Method validation near Fig. 12: approximately 2.1 s for PPO inference
baseline.training_time: not stated; Method validation says 100 RL episodes with reward convergence around 70 episodes
baseline.quality_metric: Method validation, Table 5: volume fraction, maximum displacement, maximum von Mises stress, compliance; FEA after SDF smoothing described near Figs. 9 and 11
baseline.quality_gap: Abstract: up to 40% weight reduction relative to conventional methods; corresponding classical compliance and volume fraction not stated

R1.evidence: Method validation near Fig. 12: PPO and SIMP times are compared, but no matched quality, volume fraction, or evaluation budget for those timed results is shown.

R2.evidence: Method validation near Fig. 12 and Method details: SIMP timing is given without solver, hardware or iteration information sufficient to establish an R2 failure criterion.

R3.evidence: Method validation near Fig. 12: an inference-time speed claim is made; neither training cost nor ToD data generation cost is quantified or amortized.

R4.evidence: Method validation, Table 5 and text near Figs. 9 and 11: returned design is said to pass post-smoothing FEA stress and displacement checks, but rates of failed or infeasible designs are not reported.

reporting.n_test_cases: Method validation, Table 5: one tabulated ToD output; wheel-hub case study near Fig. 13

notes: The abstract's numerical weight claim takes priority over the later numerical speed comparison under protocol 5.1. The article states post-smoothing FEA validation but provides no failure denominator. Source: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12355488/fullTextXML
